cards.prompt: Alex forwards a "Your Bank" email. Label three of its warning signs.
cards.explanation: The address after the @ isn't yourbank.example, the subject rushes you, and the button goes to yourbank-update.example.

cards.prompt: An email says you won headphones. Just pay $5 postage. What do you do?

image.alt: An email from Prize Desk, win@headphone-prizes.example. Subject: You WON wireless headphones! Pay $5 postage within 2 hours to claim. A green Pay and claim button and a drawing of headphones.

options.text: Delete it: too good to be true

cards.explanation: A prize you never entered that costs money to claim is too good to be true, and a reply goes straight to the scammer.

cards.prompt: You're expecting a parcel. A text says pay $2.50 within 1 hour. What do you do?

image.alt: A text thread headed Parcels: Missed delivery. Pay $2.50 within 1 hour: parcels-fee.example. Below, three choices: pay it; reply Which parcel?; check in the Parcels app.

cards.explanation: A fee, a rush and a strange link are warning signs, even when you're expecting a parcel: check in the company's own app.

cards.prompt: A new number texts: "It's Dad, phone broke. Send $60 now?" What do you do?

image.alt: A text from an unknown number, not in your contacts: It's Dad, phone broke. Send $60 now? Below, three choices: send it; reply Is it really you?; call Dad's saved number.

cards.explanation: It asks for money and rushes you; the saved number reaches the real Dad, while a reply goes to the new number.

cards.prompt: "Your Bank's fraud team" calls and asks for the code just texted to you. What do you do?

image.alt: A call from an unknown number, 1:05 in: Read me the code we just sent, to stop the payment. Below, three choices: read out the code; ask them to say my name first; hang up and call the number on my card.

options.text: Ask them to say my name first
Hang up and call the number on my card

cards.explanation: A code lets them sign in as you, and knowing your name proves nothing: hang up and call a number you already have.

cards.prompt: A page with a padlock asks for your card PIN. What do you do?

image.alt: A browser page with a padlock and the address cardcheck.example/verify. It shows a Your Bank logo and one box, Card PIN, with a Confirm button.

options.text: Check the logo, then type it
Close it: banks never ask this

cards.explanation: A padlock only means scrambled on the way, a logo can be copied, and a real bank never asks for your PIN on a web page.

cards.prompt: Your Bank's real address is yourbank.example. Sort each address.
cards.explanation: Only the name just before the ending counts, and it must be exactly yourbank.
